items.description: Eighteen vendor-neutral technology concepts (server rack, router, database, storage disk, cloud, API connector, laptop, mobile phone, processor, AI model, security lock, security key, code terminal, container, user identity, settings, software bug, version branch) mapped to 15 archetypes.

items.name: domain-technology-objects-2d
items.title: Technology SVG Objects
items.description: Vendor-neutral 2D SVG illustrations for every technology kind, composed from the shared illustration toolkit with themeable tokens and an accessible frame.

items.name: video-platform-presets
items.title: Social Video Platform Presets
items.description: Versioned YouTube, Shorts, TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and LinkedIn export dimensions, timing and safe-area guidance.

items.name: scene-template-foundation
items.title: Semantic Scene Template Foundation
items.description: Shared data-only validation, deterministic frame evaluation, orthographic globe projection, and responsive 2D/2.5D scene compositions for 24 typed explainer and cinematic scene recipes.

items.name: place-shaped-image-reveal
items.title: Place-Shaped Image Reveal Scene
items.description: Frame-addressable place silhouette reveal: a caller-licensed boundary traced in a place-centred orthographic projection, photographs revealed inside it and pinned to where they were taken, with a required not-an-aerial-view disclosure.

items.name: relief-map-expedition
items.title: Relief-Map Expedition Scene
items.description: Frame-addressable relief map: a Terrarium elevation model drawn as a WebGL heightfield with baked oblique sun, cast shadows and sky occlusion, one overhead-to-oblique descent, a route draped on the surface and a labelled destination hold, with declared vertical exaggeration.

items.name: orbit-world
items.title: Orbit World Scene
items.description: Frame-addressable lit-globe journey: opens over the planet's illuminated limb, orbits to real locations and draws great-circle routes on the surface behind a travelling head, then holds the destination with collision-free labels. Three.js day/night globe with terminator, ocean specular, clouds and atmosphere; orthographic 2D fallback for no WebGL and reduced motion.

items.name: page-turn-story
items.title: Page-Turn Story Scene
items.description: Frame-addressable book scene: an open hardcover on a lit desk, a leaf that peels at its corner, bends around a fixed spine with real thickness, normals and soft shadows, and lands on the next illustrated spread. Optional Three.js bending-page mesh with a 2.5D fallback; spreads, turn cues, paper, binding, desk, light and camera are configurable.

items.name: timeline-journey
items.title: Timeline Journey Scene
items.description: Frame-addressable archival history sequence: a time anchor, dated plates reached by motivated moves (truck along time, match cut on focus, dissolve, cut), Ken Burns toward each subject, a rolling Intl year readout (BCE-capable), a proportional or even rail with playhead, legible source lines and a contact-sheet summary of the elapsed span.

items.name: follow-subject-through-sections
items.title: Follow Subject Through Sections Scene
items.description: Frame-addressable journey: one recognizable subject (media or a host rig) carried through distinct parallax worlds with motivated transitions (occluder wipe, whip pan, camera carry, match cut), continuous screen position, direction, scale and light, and a contact landing at the destination.

items.name: nature-world-identity-reveal
items.title: Nature-World Identity Reveal Scene
items.description: Real 3D jungle (Three.js, optional renderer slot): scanned CC0 undergrowth, HDRI and low back-sun, depth of field, bloom; with a 2.5D fallback. Frame-addressable identity reveal: one dolly camera walks past caller depth-plane cutouts into a clearing, then a sun shaft through the canopy finds a caller-supplied mark standing as a grounded object (contact and cast shadow, thickness, rim light), with optional kinetic wordmark and line.

items.name: illustrated-book-into-living-world
items.title: Illustrated Book into Living World Scene
items.description: Frame-addressable book scene: a tactile open book on a table, a curved 24-strip page turn about the spine, then a push into the portal illustration that dissolves into the living world it depicts, registered by sharing one box and aspect.

items.name: frame-accurate-clip
items.title: Frame Accurate Clip
items.description: Deterministic footage: maps every output frame to an exact source frame (trim, rate, reverse, freezes, time remap, variable frame rate), reframes per output, and draws through capability-advertising adapters (image sequence, procedural, per-frame-verified browser video, or your own decoder) with visible errors instead of substitutes.

items.name: interaction-choreography
items.title: Interaction Choreography
items.description: Pure frame-addressable choreography for actors handling shared objects: gaze, reach, grasp, carry, place and release, with contact events, reach checks and named timing presets. Renderer-neutral and free of Three.js.

items.name: shot-bake
items.title: Shot Bake
items.description: Resolves interaction choreography, character state and a CC1 camera into one per-frame JSON document for an offline renderer. Run it offline: CC1 uses Three.js math.

items.name: shot-list-editor
items.title: Shot List Editor
items.description: Reorder shots and edit their type and purpose, with keyboard moves, per-shot diagnostics and translatable labels. Owns no timing and no renderer knowledge.

items.name: crayon-storybook
items.title: Material-native Crayon Storybook & Scene Engine
items.description: Reusable deterministic wax deposition and textured paper for JSON-authored illustrated film scenes. Original storybook art plus generic paths, contours, multi-line readable captions, authored camera motion, held-pose object animation, seeded pressure variation, and frame-addressed FilmStage slots in multiple ratios.

items.name: riso-print
items.title: Risograph Spot-Ink Printing
items.description: Two- or three-plate spot-ink compositor with absolute-frame printing, multiply overprint, fixed registration, halftone screens, paper grain, a sheet-feed transition, and a native incoming spot-ink overprint scene bridge. Authored original SVG plates render through existing FilmStage slots; no alternate renderer or clock. Adds source-native continuously graded AM ink dots, paper-fixed micro-irregularity, and optional custom SVG contour clipping.

items.name: riso-character
items.title: Risograph Character Rigs & Source-Contour Model Sheets (RISO7)
items.description: Art-directed 2D print character rigs with paper knockouts, authored facial expressions, FK/IK, SVG curve-accurate proportion meshes, concave triangulation and printable per-character reference sheets.

items.name: watercolour-brush
items.title: Watercolour & Pressure Brush
items.description: WM1 authored brush geometry and watercolor/ink deposition: pressure-width ribbons, tapered tips, stable bristle splitting, fixed-paper pigment granulation, separate diffusion/absorption/dry phases, reduced motion and exact absolute-frame seeking. SVG material renderer binds through existing FilmStage slots; no alternate clock or heavyweight dependency.

items.name: watercolour-wet-paper
items.title: Watercolour Wet Paper & Pigment Transport (WM4)
items.description: Shared paper-space finite-volume watercolor study: multiple wet pigments mix across one conservative grid, then sediment and dry into permanent, seeded, frame-addressable colors. Bounded CPU reference solver, SVG adapter, 16:9/9:16 FilmStage sample and interactive material parameters. Qualitative watercolor physics rather than calibrated spectral pigment.

items.name: watercolour-illustration
items.title: Art-directed Watercolor Illustration & Motion
items.description: WC9 original-source SVG illustration director: safe semantic group/path graph, rooted local pivots, absolute-frame keyframes, differentiated transparent watercolor/line/drybrush marks and optional shared wet-paper underpainting. Arbitrary subject authoring is supported through a bounded portable JSON contract.

items.name: watercolour-actor
items.title: Watercolour Character Staging
items.description: WM3 reusable frame-addressed animated character actor stage: feet-anchored gait and shadow, paper-space watercolour part material, on-twos cadence, actual existing character rig/cues for gestures, gaze, blinking and speech; portrait and landscape compatible.

items.name: painted-composition
items.title: Painted Composition / Arbitrary Watercolour Art
items.description: WM2 material-native watercolor scene composer. Original arbitrary SVG silhouette washes with authored paint gestures, stable granulation, wet spread, pigment-edge pooling, reserved paper highlights, optional secondary pigment and detail lines; ordered WM1 brush strokes and masked source image layers. Frame-seek deterministic, portable 16:9/9:16 FilmStage integration; original demo scenes for nature, architecture, scientific and product illustration.

items.name: ink-brush
items.title: Material-Native Ink Brush (INK1)
items.description: Frame-addressed brush marks with pressure, pace, bristle splits, and native paper-space pigment/water deposition with adjustable bleed, absorption, dry-down and stable seek. Includes a legacy SVG comparison renderer.

items.name: shodo-calligraphy
items.title: Shodō Brush Calligraphy (SHO1)
items.description: Japanese brush calligraphy written by a simulated hand and brush: every stroke is 始筆 (打ち込み, 蔵鋒, 露鋒) → 送筆 with 転折 turns → 終筆 (止め/垂露, 懸針, 撥ね, 払い) and 点, each a generated move with tunable press, hold and reach; measured technique checks on the rendered ink; configurable script (kaisho, gyōsho, sōsho), speed, pressure, width, width decay, entry angle, tremor and hairline links; brush size, hair spring and bristle lanes; ink colour, strength, colour-strength decay, water, load and re-dipping, per-stroke vermilion 朱墨; deterministic paper raster with contact-saturating deposit, dwell pooling, bristle-lane kasure, fibre-gated nijimi and wet sheen; hanshi with a faint vermilion kentei grid; a 3D bamboo fude whose lean and height follow the writing (stands up to press, leans into travel, lifts straight; 直筆 to 側筆), with a bending, ink-soaked tuft, cast shadow, motion blur and a side-view profile; any kanji or kana from pinned KanjiVG stroke data loaded at run time (not bundled) with layout rules measured on 411 teacher models (結構法), kaisho form rules and joins (接筆); original offline glyphs; scanned CC0 bamboo and wood textures and a FilmStage slot. Pure absolute-frame evaluation.

items.name: universal-rig
items.title: Universal Rig (RIG1)
items.description: Style-agnostic 2D rigs for people, dogs, horses, cats, songbirds, butterflies, koi, dragons, modern and vintage cars, bicycles with riders, locomotives, planes, helicopters, hot-air balloons, ships and clocks: a JSON bone hierarchy with material-role parts and procedural drivers (IK gaits with real footfall orders, toe roll and planted feet, side-view projected wingbeats, IK reaches, suspension springs, lights and indicators, turns in depth, rolling and skidding wheels, crank linkages, emitters, pendulums, clock hands, blinks and talk), evaluated purely from the frame, painted in six film looks on ones or twos with a tracking camera over world-anchored ground.

items.name: human-anatomy
items.title: Human Anatomy Framework (ANAT1)
items.description: Style-neutral, measured human for drawing realistic people in any art style (proportions, poses, faces, hands, depth, shading): a morphable, posable 3D body (CC0 MakeHuman lattice: sex, age 1–90, muscle, weight, height, ancestry; 57-bone skeleton; 47 named anthropometric landmarks) calibrated against ANSUR II adult measurements and CDC growth curves; clinical joint angles clamped to AAOS/CDC ranges with a pose and hand-pose library; tape-measure sections and ANSUR-named measurements; a camera that renders a HumanFrame (depth-sorted shaded triangles, visible contours with weight hints, light/shadow terminators, landmarks, joints) plus a software rasteriser for clay, five-band value, cel and silhouette surfaces; a MediaPipe-based 3D face study fitted to published facial norms with feature loops and lid-clipped irises; hair (measured fibre, density, growth and whorl data; a strand generator with anatomical hairline, parting, flow, eight curl types, clumping and collision; melanin-based hair colour, greying and Marschner highlights; brows and lashes); skin colour (Monk Skin Tone scale, ITA°, measured skin scattering, shade ramps with subsurface red at the terminator, regional colour zones) and iris colour; canon checks, surface-anatomy notes, age changes and a curated public-domain reference board. Beautiful faces from the attractiveness research (averageness, symmetry, femininity, measured eye, lip and face-breadth values, Pallett's 36% and 46% ratios; the golden ratio face claims checked and reported, not used) and a CPU portrait renderer (subsurface skin scattering, shadowed key light, occlusion, ray-traced eyes with iris and catchlight, lashes, brows, strand hair, expressions).

items.name: art-foundations
items.title: Art Foundations (shared)
items.description: Shared pieces of the art-foundation frameworks (ANIM1 animals, FLORA1 plants): points and outlines wound one way, smooth closed curves, tubes and ellipses as path data, a seeded random stream, graded ranges, sounds, references and style-index record types, a person to show scale outlined through ANAT1's measured landmarks, and the character-sheet card, swatch list and to-scale chart.

items.name: animal-anatomy
items.title: Animal Anatomy Framework (ANIM1)
items.description: Style-neutral animals for drawing the same creature in any art style: sixteen body plans (bears, dogs and foxes, cats, pigs, deer and cattle, horses, hares, mice, weasels, monkeys, five bird plans, fish) fixing foot posture, side-view construction (trunk, chest depth, leg clearance, head, muzzle, neck, tail, leg segments, back line, limb girth, waist, head carriage, ears), gaits, rearing, the parts every member has, coat regions and footfall; 23 Japanese folklore species (moon bear, wild boar, fox, tanuki, wolf, Shiba, cat, hare, macaque, sika, black cattle, Kiso horse, weasel, mouse, crane, heron, crow, pheasant, sparrow, goshawk, mandarin duck, kingfisher, koi) with graded size and proportion ranges (reported, measured, estimated) and sources, face proportions, coat type and length by region, palettes painted by region, tip, band or eye mask, markings, seasonal and juvenile variants, sounds (catalog ids or search terms), culture, public-domain and CC0 references and where each is already drawn in the library; one shared gait table (walk, amble, trot, canter, transverse and rotary gallop, half-bound) after Muybridge and Hildebrand, with footfall diagrams, speeds by dynamic similarity and stride times by body mass; a construction that poses any species standing or at any point of a stride with planted feet that never slide; silhouette, construction, colour-map and fur-map painters; proportion checks that measure any drawing or rig against the species' ranges; and a character sheet with size against a person.

items.name: plant-anatomy
items.title: Plant Anatomy Framework (FLORA1)
items.description: Style-neutral plants for drawing the same tree, bamboo, flower or grass in any art style. Thirteen growth forms (spire conifers, pines, broadleaf, blossom trees, weeping, layered, bamboo, shrubs, climbers, herbs, irises, water plants, grasses) built after Rex Vicat Cole's The Artistic Anatomy of Trees (1915): bud plans (opposite, alternate, spiral, whorled), excurrent, sympodial and forking leaders, crown envelopes, branch angles, droop and upturned tips, foliage manners (needle pads, scale sprays, clouds, hanging strands, layered sprays, leaf fans, blades, swords, floating leaves) and widths by Leonardo's rule. 24 Japanese plants (black and red pine, cedar, hinoki, mountain cherry, plum, willow, maple, madake bamboo, ginkgo, zelkova, camphor, persimmon, peach, wisteria, camellia, chrysanthemum, kakitsubata iris, lotus, susuki, reed, paulownia, morning glory, rice) with graded sizes and sources, leaves, flowers, fruit and bark, a calendar of leaf, bloom, autumn colour and fruit, seasonal colours, sounds, culture, public-domain and CC0 references (Flora Japonica, Hokusai, Hiroshige, Kōrin) and where each is already drawn. A seeded generator grows any plant for any month and wind; leaf, flower, fruit and bark shape generators; silhouette, construction and colour painters; data and proportion checks; and a character sheet with the four seasons and size against a person. Crown and trunk in detail (plant-crown.ts, TreePaint): foliage tufts built from the species' leaf shapes, lit on the sun side and dark beneath; light filtered through the crown (Beer–Lambert); a foliage colour ladder measured on CC0/PD tree photos; sky holes at the measured gap fraction, fringed by leaves; edge leaves, needle bursts and blossom petals; willow strand leaves; cylinder-shaded trunks and limbs with bark wrapped round them, root flare and limbs swelling into the trunk; wet bark; detail levels for scenes; physical wind sway (cantilever frequency, hanging-chain willow twigs).

items.name: sky-weather
items.title: Sky and Weather Framework (SKY1)
items.description: Style-neutral weather and sky for any art style: the Beaufort scale with sea and land signs; rain, snow, hail, fog, mist and haze classes; drop size spectra (Marshall-Palmer), fall speeds (Atlas 1973), drop shapes (Brandes 2002), slant in wind, streak length at a shutter, visibility and Koschmieder distance fading; the ten WMO cloud genera with heights, looks, WMO element widths and 1896 Cloud Atlas plates, drawn as layered shapes (cauliflower cumulus, anvil cumulonimbus, cirrus wisps, rows of altocumulus, rolls, layers with rain curtains) and set in perspective as cloud decks; sky phases by sun elevation with sampled palettes and the CIE overcast sky; sun elevation and shadow length; lightning stroke timing and branching channels, thunder delay and rainbow geometry. One weather state feeds the environmental-effects renderers at real speeds. A weather scene, cloud atlas and reference sheet; every value graded reported, measured or estimated with sources. Cumulus in detail (sky-cumulus.ts): a tree of rising thermals, lumps on lumps (cauliflower), light by sun azimuth per mass, shading ladders measured from CC0/PD cloud photos, backlit silver linings on the true silhouette, and turrets that rise and fade at measured updraft speeds. Rendered skies: a single-scattering atmosphere (Rayleigh, Mie from visibility, ozone; Hillaire 2020 constants) and all ten genera as volumes of cloud water or ice built from their physics (extinction from water content and effective radius, WMO element widths, Kelvin-Helmholtz billow rows, cirrus fall streaks bent by shear, 22 and 46 degree ice halos, translucent altostratus, ragged nimbostratus with scud and rain, cumulonimbus towers, anvil, overshooting top and mammatus), lit by marched sunlight, multiple-scattering octaves and two-stream diffusion, with aerial perspective, cloud shadows and camera metering; CloudSky and RenderedCloudAtlas.

items.name: water
items.title: Water Framework (WATER1)
items.description: Style-neutral water for any art style: the WMO sea state code; the fully developed sea a wind raises (Pierson-Moskowitz: significant height, peak period, wavelength, crest speed) with whitecap cover (Monahan & O'Muircheartaigh); dispersion in deep and shallow water; a seeded sea surface of short-crested third-order Stokes waves to sample anywhere and any time, float heave and pitch, and particle orbits; wave limits (H/L 0.142, 120 degree crest, breaking at 0.8 depth); breakers by the Iribarren number (spilling, plunging, collapsing, surging) drawn in cross-section at any stage with foam, a plunging lip on its ballistic arc and the air of the tube; Kelvin wakes (19.47 degrees, transverse spacing 2 pi V^2/g) and ripple rings; Fresnel reflectance, the mirror rule, sun glitter from Cox-Munk slopes and colour through depth; sine-generated meanders 11 widths long; water colours measured off CC0 and public-domain photographs. A sea scene (colours from Fresnel and the sky, glints only where a facet mirrors the sun), true-scale seas by wind, breaker, wake, ripple, reflection and meander figures and a reference sheet; every value graded with sources. Breakers and foam in detail (breakerDetail): flow lines in the face, a translucent teal lip from water's absorption, a lit tube, whitewater with bubbles over an aerated plume, foam lace, spray and spindrift blown off the crest, with colours measured from surf photos; the sea scene leaves foam lace that fades at a rate measured from surf video, streaked along the wind in gales. A rendered open sea (water-ocean.ts): JONSWAP and Pierson-Moskowitz spectra with Hasselmann spreading summed by FFT in three cascades (Tessendorf), choppy crests, whitecaps where the surface folds at Monahan's measured cover with fading foam, slopes calibrated to Cox-Munk, Fresnel reflection of SKY1's sky and clouds, Cox-Munk sun glitter, the blue light back out of deep water from absorption and Morel's backscatter, turquoise backlit crests and haze; OceanView and SeaByBeaufort.

items.name: terrain
items.title: Terrain and Landforms Framework (GEO1)
items.description: The ground in any art style: twelve landforms by how they formed (fold ranges, glacial horns, U- and V-valleys, strato-, shield and cinder volcanoes, mesas and buttes, barchan dunes, scree, sea cliffs, rolling hills) with their reported slopes, reliefs, profiles and drawing notes; the angle of repose of loose material; snowlines and treelines by latitude; ground-cover albedo; the rules of distance. Heightfields for each landform worn by hydraulic erosion (droplets cutting gullies and laying fans) and thermal erosion (scree at its angle of repose), and a renderer: snow above the snowline (lower on shaded slopes, only where it can hold), rock on steep faces, scree, meadow and forest by the treeline, sand, ash and water, under SKY1's physical atmosphere with terrain shadows, aerial perspective and camera metering. TerrainView (worker, cached), LandformProfile and GeoSheet; every value graded reported, measured or estimated with sources.

items.name: materials
items.title: Materials Framework (MATL1)
items.description: Style-neutral materials for any art style and any renderer: 56 materials (metals, rust and patina, lacquer, wood, bamboo, tatami, thatch, paper, plaster, ceramics and roof tile, stone, earth, organic, glass, ice, liquids) with linear-light albedo or metal reflectance, metalness, roughness, refractive index, surface variation and painting notes; 36 from the CC0 Physically Based database with its cited measurements, 18 measured off CC0 ambientCG colour maps, red and black lacquer off a CC0 Met photograph. Value (CIE L*) and a value ladder, F0 and highlight spread, standard PBR parameters for three.js, glTF or Blender, wet darkening after Angstrom and Lekner-Dorf, and weathering tracks (copper to verdigris by air, iron to rust, wood to grey, bamboo, tatami, paper, Negoro lacquer wear). Textures (materials-texture.ts) built from each material's structure at real size and calibrated to measured CC0 ambientCG statistics: wood as a log cut into boards (rings with year-to-year widths, earlywood and latewood, flat-sawn arches, knots with bark rings, weathered earlywood eroding at the reported rates), bamboo culms with nodes, bloom and smoke staining, tatami rushes in 1.5 cm wales between warp grooves (JAS, JAANUS), trimmed thatch stalk ends, washi and kraft fibres, cardboard flutes, leather grain, grass, granite crystals in measured mineral shares, marble veins, slate, sand, salt and snow grains, concrete voids, asphalt aggregate, clay cracks, JIS brick walls, plaster, ibushi tile, rust, patina, lacquer and metal finishes. A CPU renderer (materials-render.ts) shows each as a ball in a studio or a tile under raking light, with soft shadows, cavity occlusion, subsurface scattering, refraction through clear materials, nacre interference, glints, brushed anisotropy and wet looks. Rendered swatches (MaterialSwatch, MaterialStudy with a scale bar), flat material balls, weathering strips, wet-and-dry tiles and a reference sheet; every value graded with sources.

items.name: costume
items.title: Clothing and Costume Framework (COSTUME1)
items.description: Clothing and costume of the whole world found by tags, not by period alone: UN M49 regions (hierarchical), ISO 3166 countries and cultures, year ranges and named eras (Heian, Edo, Joseon, Ming, Qing, Victorian and more), worn by women, men or all, roles, occasions, body slot, cut, fabrics and climate. 74 garments across East, South and South-east Asia, Western Asia, Africa, Europe, the Americas and Oceania, each with local names, a sourced description, graded period, drawing notes and where the library already draws it; 33 outfits for a place, year and wearer; a query engine (findGarments, findOutfits, tag strings), facet counts, a world-by-time matrix, front-view garment constructions on the measured ANAT1 person (sleeves, skirts, trousers, bands, drapes, hats) and a reference sheet. Drape and detail (costume-drape.ts): fabric folds from each cloth's stiffness (bending lengths within Peirce's measured range), pipe folds from obi, sash and waistband, waved hems, catenary swags on draped cloth, elbow and sleeve folds, hooped skirts; necklines and collars (crossed collar left over right, mandarin collar with knot buttons, lapels with shirt, tie and buttons, placket, square neck), kimono obiage, obijime, lining and hanging sleeves, hakama pleats, kilt apron, sari pleats; tartan, stripe, kente and dyed-motif patterns.

items.name: facial-expressions
items.title: Facial Expressions Framework (EXPR1)
items.description: Style-neutral facial expressions for any art style, built on ANAT1's measured face. FACS action units (names and muscles from the Facial Action Coding System) become displacement fields on the 468-point face, with a dropping jaw, closing lids, gaze and head pose. The seven EMFACS emotion prototypes (happiness, sadness, surprise, fear, anger, disgust, contempt; reported) and drawing extras (polite smile, laughter, crying, shyness, pain, sleep, determination, the kabuki mie glare; estimated), with blending. Style-neutral features (brows, lids, cheeks, nose, mouth corners, width and opening, in eye widths) any style can map onto its own drawing; the creases each unit makes, drawn as lines or as kumadori in the role's colour; a nearest-emotion check that a drawn face reads as intended; Noh tilt and kumadori colour and pattern notes; a line-study painter, an atlas and per-emotion sheets.

items.name: makeup
items.title: Makeup and Beauty Framework (MAKEUP1)
items.description: Makeup and beauty for any face in any art style, grounded in graded evidence and learned from openly licensed photographs. A 31-zone atlas on the 468-point face mesh (shared with a Python photo pipeline): foundation, concealer, corrector, cheek, temple, jaw and nose contour, five highlights, bronzer, five blush placements, lid, crease, outer V, inner corner, lower lash line, liner and wing, brow fill on the brow map (peak at 71% of the eye width), lips, liner, gradient and gloss, anchored to vertices and sized in eye widths so it follows each face. 14 products as pigment films (stain to opaque paint, Kubelka-Munk simplified) and 8 finishes (matte to glitter). Colour: CIEDE2000, ITA and an undertone split from measured cheek hue (Xiao et al. 2017), foundation matching with the measured healthy shift (Stephen et al. 2009), concealer and correctors, contour, bronzer and highlight by depth and undertone, blush and lip families, eyeshadow complements by iris, brows from hair. 12 looks as colour rules (no-makeup, fresh dewy, soft glam, sculpted, classic red, smoky eye, sun-kissed, igari, monochrome rose, grooming, maiko); face-shape and eye-shape placement rules; designMakeup with reasons, checkMakeup (contour stops before the iris, blush above the nose base, light above shadow, wing angle, foundation match, lip contrast against learned ranges, brow peak); makeupPaint for ANAT1 portraits (films lit without subsurface scattering, finish, shimmer flakes, mascara, brow colour) and paintPhoto for any photograph with MediaPipe landmarks (frequency separation keeps the skin's texture); face charts, undertone plane, evidence and learned-data tables. Learned data: bare-skin prior, makeup effects, placement, facial contrast and beauty correlations from the Face Research Lab London Set (CC BY 4.0) and CC0 portraits.

items.name: editorial-collage
items.title: Editorial Paper Collage (COLLAGE1)
items.description: Data-driven newsroom-explainer paper collage: torn and cut paper with white fibre cores and lift shadows, amplitude-modulated halftone shading and archival-print filter, tape, boiling marker and highlighter strokes, condensed headlines on pasted-up slips with measured word layout, paper maps (Natural Earth land) with routes and pins, red string, jointed paper-puppet characters with walk/run/talk/gesture actions, stop-motion cadence and boil, parallax rostrum camera, object kit, real-photo registers (cut-outs with alpha-following torn sticker borders, halftone/duotone print, Ken Burns archival prints, document scans with OCR-placed highlights and spotlight, flat-colour and dark slate boards, shaded-relief maps, label/year boxes, chapter captions) and a paper-tear transition. Pure absolute-frame evaluation; JSON scenes validated with path-specific errors.

items.name: ukiyoe-handscroll
items.title: Ukiyo-e Woodblock & Handscroll (UKIYO1)
items.description: Data-driven ukiyo-e woodblock-print and emaki handscroll film engine: colour blocks assigned to impressions light-to-dark with kento misregistration, bokashi gradients, wood-grain (itame) and baren-mottle textures, carved key-block lines and a washi skin; a print-pass reveal (key block, then colours); generated motifs (sky incl. great-wave horizon bokashi, great-wave Fuji, sea, great-wave crest with Prussian face, flecks and hooked claw rows, pine, cherry, willow and plum grown by FLORA1 (whorled needle-pad tiers, branches of elbows with blossom clouds, arching curtains, flowers on dark wood), reeds, rock, suyari-gasumi clouds, sun, moon, townhouse incl. fukinuki-yatai cutaway, pagoda, torii, bridge, boats, lanterns, pier, fields, folktale peach that splits open, terraced rice paddies young/ripe/flooded); weather and particles (Hiroshige rain, snow, petals, leaves, fireflies, birds, ripples, fireworks, spray); articulated Edo figures with costumes, patterns, props and 20 layered actions, faces whose fourteen expressions come from the facial expressions framework (EXPR1), including oni (horns, fangs, wild mane, tiger loincloth, kanabo); folktale creature rigs: fox and nine-tailed kitsune with foxfire, tanuki (upright drumming), dog, cat, rabbit, crane, heron, crow, pheasant, sparrow and a serpentine dragon with pearl, with henge transform puffs; one scene-wide wind field; handscroll camera with parallax; cartouche, seal and caption text; gold mist-band (kasumi) transition. Pure absolute-frame evaluation; JSON scenes validated with path-specific errors.

items.name: ukiyoe-episode
items.title: Ukiyo-e Folktale Episode Template (UKIYO1)
items.description: Turns a folktale written as UKIYO1 shots and the narration over each into one FD1 film document for YouTube (16:9) and Shorts (9:16): a title printed block by block with a cartouche and seal, gold-mist (kasumi) transitions, narration as the film caption track sized per output inside the platform safe area, an end card that keeps the end-screen area clear, recorded sound effects placed on what the picture does (footsteps on every foot plant, blows on their contact frames) and panned and distanced from where their source stands on screen, a pre-render script check (reading speed, two-line fit per output, caption gaps, scene text out of the caption band, end-card length) and an .srt export for upload.

items.name: film-look
items.title: Film Look
items.description: How a film feels, as explicit, deterministic numbers: a colour grade (tone curve, balance, split toning, channel mixer, posterising), the texture of a film stock or a video format (grain, halation, bloom, anamorphic streaks, gate weave, flicker, vignette, light leaks, blinds, scan lines, tracking noise, colour bleed, mattes), frame cadence (on twos, step printed), camera behaviour (locked, drift, float, handheld, a push-in at the story turn), a lens choice for 3D shots, a 3D lighting mood, type and sound mood. Twelve presets and eight mood words that move them in researched directions; `FilmLookLayer` draws a look over any scene with one SVG filter and a few layers, the same in any frame order.

items.name: ink-shanshui-landscape
items.title: Chinese Ink Shanshui Landscape Animator
items.description: Code-drawn 16:9 Chinese ink landscapes with layered sepia mountain washes, cunfa cliff lines, original pine, willow and bamboo art, arched bridges, water, mist and parallax; three compositional presets, deterministic absolute-frame animation, no raster references or external runtime dependencies.

items.name: ink-wash-core
items.title: Chinese Ink Wash Brush and Paper
items.description: Standalone material-native ink brush renderer with pressure-shaped silhouettes, ink-loaded side-brush gradient, dry-brush splits, wet paper spread, procedural rock texture and reduced-motion final holds; frame addressed and no WebGL dependencies.

items.name: ink-wash-film
items.title: Chinese Ink Wash Film Composition
items.description: Composable ink-wash directing grammar for any authored footage, illustrations, diagrams, titles, and actor layers: five looks, ink bloom/brush entrances, parallax handscroll camera and FilmDocument shot adapter.

items.name: ink-wash-character
items.title: Chinese Ink Character Performance
items.description: Paper-native, independently articulated 2D/2.5D ink-wash actor rendering over the existing validated character rig: per-part capillary fringe and paper-tooth edges, deterministic acting tracks, visemes, blink, gaze, gestures, props and optional tints, no new timeline or WebGL.

items.name: ink-figure-craft
items.title: Chinese Ink Figure Brushwork
items.description: Validated authored Chinese ink figure folds (floating silk-thread, layered wash, dry flying-white), pressure-native SVG geometry attached to existing CharacterPresenter part rigs; stable seed, detail and pigment controls.

items.name: ink-actor-director
items.title: Chinese Ink Character Motion Director
items.description: Deterministic C1 continuous route blocking, planted-foot gait, 2-bone character IK, and independent cloth/arm/head correction tracks on the existing character timeline.

items.name: ink-figure-motion
items.title: Chinese Ink Figure Cloth Motion
items.description: Reusable frame-pure cloth follow-through. Bakes subtly moving independent hem and cuff corrections on top of an approved INK4 route; deterministic absolute-frame sampling, bounded intensity, no replacement clock.

items.name: ink-wash-ensemble
items.title: Chinese Ink Character Ensemble
items.description: Deterministic, identity-preserving multi-character Chinese ink acting: independently staged canonical ink rigs, attention/interaction beats, gaze targeting, ordered depth and explicit foot-separation/reach audits on the existing film timeline. Compose with ink-actor-director for continuous paths and IK.

items.name: film-cards
items.title: Film Cards
items.description: The typographic scenes of ads and short explainers, for a film document's `card` scenes: a hook headline with one word in the brand colour, a numbered list that arrives point by point with progress, a before-and-after or myth-and-fact versus with a per-line strike, a quote with a star rating, and the end card with the brand's mark, a line and one call to action; plus the brand's corner bug. Each enters fast and then holds still while it is read, keeps inside the output's safe area, lightens the brand colour until it reads as text and picks a readable ink for brand fills. Timing comes from reading speed, and `inspectCard` reports cards too short to read.

items.name: film-document
items.title: Film Document
items.description: One JSON file for a whole film: ordered scene recipes, object stories, ray worlds and React Three Fiber 3D shots, transitions, captions, audio lanes and output sizes. Compiles through the existing compilers, with every problem reported as a JSON Pointer and a fix hint, and a generated JSON Schema.

items.name: ad-formats
items.title: Ad Formats
items.description: A short ad brief becomes a complete, checked film document in one of six structures: hook-body-close, problem-solution, before-after, three-reasons, myth-vs-fact and social-proof. The hook opens the film, the brand is seen from the first frame and closes it with one call to action, an optional 3D product hero turn sits after the body, scene lengths come from reading time, and the story fields (the question the hook opens, the turn that answers it, how each scene follows the last) are filled in so the film's story, pacing and ad checks pass. Outputs map to vertical, landscape and square presets.

items.name: race-recipes
items.title: Race Recipes
items.description: A car at speed on a track, in React Three Fiber. Track Pass: a low trackside camera on a long lens pans with the car as it approaches, passes level with the lens and races away; or a camera rides alongside while the track streams past. Photographed asphalt with kerbs and edge lines, grass verges and guardrails whose posts show speed, lit by a daylight sky whose brightest point places the sun, with a ring of hazy mountains kilometres away (generated, or any glTF terrain tile) as a far horizon for pans and chases. Any glTF car with named wheels: they turn by distance over radius and smear into a shutter blur that follows the film's playback rate, so they sharpen inside a speed ramp's hold. Pure functions of the frame.

items.name: screen-demo
items.title: Screen Demo
items.description: Real UI, as screenshots or as live React, operated by a choreographed cursor: moves timed by Fitts' law on a minimum-jerk path, clicks with a dwell, press and ripple, typing with a human rhythm and a caret, and scrolling. A camera frames the active region a moment before each action, holds one framing for nearby controls, crops in to follow the work in a portrait output, cuts instead of gliding under reduced motion, and steps back at the end; callouts ring the target and name the change in a lower-third band. Live UI is shown inert with its transitions off, so every frame is exact. Checks report unknown targets and states, unlicensed or wrongly shaped screenshots, screenshots enlarged past their pixels, rushed actions and results not held long enough to see.

items.name: motion-chart
items.title: Guided Motion Chart
items.description: Bubbles moving over time, placed by two measures and sized by a third, with a large time counter behind them, and the guidance that makes them followable: before each event playback slows to a hold, a cue in a stable caption band says what to watch, the other bubbles dim and grey, a ring marks the subject, then the change plays at a third of the speed leaving a trail and a note says what it meant. Labels take the first clear place round their bubbles. Log or linear axes, colour groups, light and dark. Checks refuse an event without a cue (animated charts are followed only when primed), overlapping events, events outside the data and scenes too short for their holds; they warn on long cues, crowded labels, too many events and playback too fast to read.

items.name: annotate
items.title: Annotated Picture
items.description: The video-essay move on a picture: it drifts while it registers, then for each mark the camera stops, pushes in on a detail (or stays wide, aimed at it), and a pen draws on it, a circle, an arrow, an underline or a measuring bracket, with a few words beside it while the rest of the frame dims. Strokes are hand-drawn and seeded, so each is irregular in its own way and the same on every render; notes take the side with room at the output size, and a vertical frame aims at the marks. Checks refuse marks outside the picture, out of order or without notes, and scenes too short to read the last note; they warn on more than four marks, long notes, notes left before they can be read, a picture marked before it registers and a picture with no rights record.

items.name: draw-on
items.title: Draw-On
items.description: Line art that draws itself stroke by stroke with the pen's tip on the end of the line: ink on warm paper or chalk on a board, a faint bleed round each line, a watercolour wash that blooms in each closed outline once it is drawn, and a label that lands when its stroke is done. Strokes are points smoothed through (or kept as corners), so the pen's place is plain arithmetic; the pen lifts and travels between strokes and casts its shadow. Checks refuse strokes off the canvas or out of order and scenes that end mid-stroke or before the last label is read; they warn on a pen faster than a hand, overlapping strokes, open outlines with a wash, long labels, labels left before they are read, and labels that collide or leave the safe area in an output's shape.

items.name: title-sequence
items.title: Title Sequence
items.description: A film's opening built on one symbol for its story, in cut paper: pieces with scissor-cut edges slide in or are set down one at a time and settle, each with a paper shadow that lengthens while it is in the air, animated on twos as stop motion is, over a grained paper ground; then the title is laid in word by word, with no fade, into a box set into the symbol, and the credits after it. Checks hold it to one symbol of up to a dozen pieces, built before the title arrives, and give the title and each credit their reading time; they project each line into each output and warn when it overflows its box or leaves the safe area.

items.name: chart-morph
items.title: Chart Morph
items.description: A chart that changes from one state to the next in stages, one kind of change at a time: an axis that must grow grows first, then the values move, an axis that can shrink tightens, the rows re-sort, and the form changes (bar, dot, dumbbell, or line for ordered categories). One highlighted category keeps its colour and bold label through every stage; rows that swap places fade their names while they move. Each state's caption arrives as its change begins and holds still while it is read. Checks warn when a state asks for its changes together (motion-unstaged) and refuse dumbbells without starting values, lines over unordered categories, missing captions and scenes too short to stage.

items.name: quiz-card
items.title: Quiz Card
items.description: A quiz question for a page or a video, from one card. Interactive (Quiz): the learner picks from two to four lettered options, a native radio group, checks the pick, and sees the right option filled and ticked, a wrong pick crossed, and one line of why; value and reveal can be controlled, a quick-fire mode answers on the first pick, and retry is optional. In a film (QuizCard): the same card as a pure function of a frame, with a line that drains toward the answer and an optional guess by a presenter; it measures the box it is given, so it fits a full frame, a third of a frame and a vertical output. Nothing is marked before the answer; right and wrong are a tick and a cross as well as a colour, with a status line for screen readers; the explanation's space is held, so the card never jumps. Themes: dark, light or the design system's own tokens; glass, solid or outline surfaces; three sizes; and CSS variables for every colour, the radius, the shadow and both fonts. Checks for films refuse a missing answer or parts out of order and warn on an answer shown before the question can be read.

items.name: screen-demo-example
items.title: Screen Demo Example
items.description: A worked screen demo: a small task list built from Kumiki's Button, Input, Checkbox and Badge, drawn as a pure function of the demo's state, with measured targets and the same flow as a live-UI demo and as a four-screenshot demo. A starting point for demos of your own interface.

items.name: story-scenes-3d
items.title: Story Scenes 3D
items.description: Scenes that tell a story with real objects, light and physics, each a pure function of the frame. Shadow Reveal: coins hanging in the dark cast one clear shape, and line up into it as the camera nears the light. Chain Reaction: a cause-and-effect chain printed on growing dominoes, read and then tipped, from a deterministic bake. Physical Data: values as stacks of coins or blocks. Tabletop Story: object-story with catalog objects on a walnut table. Scale Journey: a coin to a bank in a log-space camera move, with a scale figure. Inside Out: a cut across a phone's back shows its battery, board and coil, with leader-line labels. Diorama Journey: a traveller crosses a miniature world on a plinth, station by station, under a tilt-shift blur.

items.name: film-3d-stage
items.title: Film 3D Stage
items.description: Draws the `shot-3d` scenes of a film document with the React Three Fiber recipes: the crafted phone and laptop in Kumiki's product studio (hero turn, part spotlight, exploded view, finish comparison, two-angle proof, a screen that performs, a step through the screen into a world, particles gathering into the subject), light through water, a baked flythrough, a captured place and baked physics. Pass `createShot3dRenderer(assets)` to `FilmStage` as `renderShot3d`. Asset files and the optional splat renderer are given by the app, so a film loads only what it uses.

items.name: scene-template-examples
items.title: Scene Recipe Examples
items.description: One valid, renderable example spec for each original scene recipe and for object-story, with original generated SVG assets. A starting point for authored or generated films.

items.name: rendered-text-audit
items.title: Rendered Text Audit
items.description: Read the laid-out text boxes of one rendered frame and report collisions, clipping, text outside the frame or platform safe area, and small type. Measure its pixels for text contrast, an empty frame and where a squinting eye lands. No model.

items.name: sound-catalog
items.title: Sound Catalog
items.description: Data and checks for sound files whose rights travel with them: licence, source, hash, format and the exact peak time. Refuses unknown licences, unsafe paths and impossible formats, and filters what may ship in a pack.

items.name: ray-world
items.title: Ray World Stage
items.description: A seek-exact stage for ray-traced GLSL worlds, with true motion blur, depth of field and antialiasing from averaged sub-samples. WebGL2, with no library.

items.name: ray-world-water-drop
items.title: Water Drop World
items.description: A hanging water drop with a landscape inside it. Real refraction shows your photographs upside down, the camera dives through each drop into the next place, and focus pulls back to a new drop in your last one.

items.name: ray-world-terraced-relief
items.title: Terraced Relief World
items.description: A terraced plaster island on a terracotta table, lit like a product. A river steps down its layers, and blue ice sweeps over it and retreats.

items.name: ray-world-river-flight
items.title: River Flight World
items.description: One unbroken flight up a procedural valley into a glacier tunnel, then a rewind at speed. One photograph gives it a real sky.

items.name: film-gallery
items.title: Film Gallery
items.description: A searchable wall of films. Each one loads only when a viewer presses play.

items.name: sound-design
items.title: Sound Design
items.description: Sound recipes as data: local catalog search, deterministic takes, material contacts, rooms and positions, compiled to one FFmpeg graph and an ordinary SoundEvent.

items.name: sound-mastering
items.title: Sound Mastering
items.description: Delivery profiles and checks for a finished mix: loudness, true peak, DC, clipping, clicks and loop seams.

items.name: shader-fx-model
items.title: Shader FX Model
items.description: Validated, data-only specs for six cinematic shader effects: bounded parameters, restrained treatments, and time as a pure function of the frame. No GPU code, so a film can carry effects without the renderer.

items.name: shader-fx
items.title: Shader FX
items.description: Frame-addressable cinematic shaders: mesh gradient, liquid metal, god rays, grain gradient, water and halftone dots. Seek-exact in export, with named failures and released WebGL contexts. Built on Paper Shaders (Apache-2.0).

items.name: shader-fx-moments
items.title: Shader FX Moments
items.description: Ready-made effect moments, each one job done the way studio work does it: dots that resolve into a picture, light that gathers into a mark, a chrome sting, a living still, a signature gradient and rays placed on the real light in a photograph. Each comes with its text timing and sound cues.

items.name: object-story
items.title: Object Story
items.description: Narrated scene told by persistent objects: every beat must visibly change something. Compiles arrangements, value counts, links, transfers, measured gaps, marks, a measured caption position and a stillness report; evaluates any frame purely.

items.name: audio-visual-cue
items.title: Audio Visual Cue
items.description: Joins frame-accurate visual events, narration words, music beats and sound effects; maps Blender PM2 material/impact speed to licensed audio assets with sub-frame timing. Includes WhisperX, Whisper, Gentle, MFA TextGrid, SRT/VTT and TTS timing parsers, alignment diagnostics, caption/MotionDirector bridges and FFmpeg mix manifests.

items.name: freeze-frame-focus
items.title: Freeze Frame Focus
items.description: Recipe that pauses footage or animation on an exact frame, pushes in on a tracked source-pixel annotation with a spotlight, explains it with measured callouts, then releases and resumes; refuses untracked details and reports upscaling or cropped details per output.

items.name: evidence-stage
items.title: Evidence Stage
items.description: Presents authorized photos, document excerpts and data tables with exact anchors (verified quotes, cell values, image regions), readable provenance and rights, focus beats that keep the cited target and its context in view, callouts that never cover the source, and a conclusion whose citations link back to the evidence.

items.name: map-stage
items.title: Map Stage
items.description: Caller-licensed GeoJSON-style geometry with mandatory attribution, equirectangular and orthographic projections fitted to the output, routes that draw by frame, pins with measured labels, eased location focus, and a legend and attribution that are always drawn. No geometry is bundled or fetched.

items.name: distribution-stage
items.title: Distribution Stage
items.description: Distributions from samples, bins, pre-binned counts or a closed-form normal, with exact histogram counts, checked count/density axes, probability areas from the CDF or counts, stated uncertainty intervals, seeded sampling reveal and measured labels. Refuses mislabelled axes, samples outside bins, zero-width or inverted areas, invalid levels and intervals that do not contain their estimate.

items.name: scale-comparison-stage
items.title: Scale Comparison Stage
items.description: Items of one dimension on one shared labelled linear or log scale, with exact rational unit conversions, a compare beat stating its ratio and rounding rule, and a convert beat printing its arithmetic. Labels are measured and wrapped; overlaps, mixed dimensions, unsourced real values and log bars are refused.

items.name: graph-topology-stage
items.title: Graph Topology Stage
items.description: Typed nodes and edges with deterministic layered or seeded force layouts, identity-preserving transitions keyed by id, BFS/DFS traversal in visit order, declared clusters as hulls, and weight-scaled strokes with a legend. Refuses unknown endpoints, duplicate ids, identity loss, undeclared node changes, negative weights, missing clusters and layered cycles.

items.name: code-stage
items.title: Code Stage
items.description: Measured, pre-tokenized source code that reveals line by line, focuses a line range or one token occurrence, and edits between complete revisions with fixed line slots (removed and added lines fade, changed tokens are marked). Captured terminal output shows in a reserved panel and is never executed. The font is fitted to the box and code is never truncated; tokens are supplied by the caller and checked to concatenate exactly to each line.

items.name: chart-story
items.title: Chart Story
items.description: Story beats over the existing chart renderer: one constant value axis across scenarios, zero-based bars and areas, reveals, focus and comparisons addressed by data identity, what-if scenarios that morph real layouts without inventing intermediate numbers, and a concluding claim checked against the data.

items.name: screen-surface
items.title: Screen Surface
items.description: Binds browser or app content to an existing 3D device's display mesh: a canvas sized to the display's true aspect (never stretched), frame-addressed painting that repeats exactly on seek, fitted images, projected corners for screen-space callouts, and camera-aware readability and facing checks.

items.name: domain-finance-object-review
items.title: Finance Object Reference Review
items.description: Reference URLs and review status for each finance/business 3D object; not an automatic photorealism claim.

items.name: crafted-3d-quality
items.title: 3D Asset Quality Contracts
items.description: Deterministic, renderer-free checks for physical hero asset structure and manually reviewed photo evidence metadata.

items.name: craft-part-rig
items.title: Part Rig
items.description: Deterministic posing of separately animatable named parts in any Three.js hierarchy: translate, rotate about a pivot, scale, opacity (material clones, nested fades multiply) and visibility layered over an asset's own actions.

items.name: inspectable-asset
items.title: Inspectable Asset
items.description: Renderer-neutral adapter contract for 2D/3D assets: semantic part tree, frame-addressed bounds and anchors, states and declared capabilities, with structural diagnostics, a camera-target bridge and an SVG adapter for tagged part groups.

items.name: inspectable-asset-three
items.title: Inspectable Asset (Three.js)
items.description: Inspect any HeroAsset through InspectableAsset: measured per-frame mesh bounds and anchors that follow moving parts. Existing hero assets need no changes.

items.name: domain-home-model
items.title: Home Model
items.description: Renderer-neutral house spec, presets and validated layout plus customizable interiors: floor plans (rooms tiling the footprint, connections), derived walls and doors, furniture recipes with per-room overrides, electrical, yards, walk map and room tours; service routes for ducts, line set, water and rain.

items.name: domain-home-3d
items.title: Home Kit 3D
items.description: Crafted layered 3D houses from a HouseSpec: envelope, structure and systems plus furnished interiors (partitions, interior doors, ~40 furniture/fixture kinds, appliances, lights, outlets) and yards; every room, item and moving sub-part (doors, drawers, appliance doors) a separately animatable group with frame-addressed actions; stand-alone equipment HeroAssets (condenser with fan and status light, air handler, tank and tankless water heaters with valve pivots and a display); a buildable snowman yard prop.

items.name: section-reveal
items.title: Section Reveal
items.description: Look inside intact assemblies without moving parts: isolate, ghost, sweeping section and capped section planned per absolute frame over any InspectableAsset, with explicit fallbacks and diagnostics; includes the SVG isolate/ghost adapter.

items.name: section-reveal-three
items.title: Section Reveal (Three.js)
items.description: Applies SectionReveal frames to Three.js assets: per-mesh fades, world-space clipping planes on material clones and approximate stencil caps colored from real material albedo.

items.name: semantic-callouts
items.title: Semantic Callout Layer
items.description: Labels and leaders attached to moving semantic parts: per-frame anchors from InspectableAsset, measured CJK-safe wrapping, collision-free placement around protected regions/parts, and honest visible/occluded/outside/unplaceable status; SVG overlay included.

items.name: semantic-callouts-three
items.title: Semantic Callouts (Three.js)
items.description: Exact HeroAssetViewer camera reconstruction, projection and depth-aware ray-cast occlusion for SemanticCalloutLayer.

items.name: flow-path
items.title: Flow Path
items.description: Illustrative directional flow along 2D/3D polylines or MG1 motion paths: arrows, streaks, particles, ribbon or pulse, pure per absolute frame with capped markers, seeded per-particle jitter, draw-on, reversal and honest measured-vs-illustrative magnitude; SVG renderer included.

items.name: flow-path-three
items.title: Flow Path (Three.js)
items.description: Three.js FlowPath adapter: draw-on tube track, fixed-capacity instanced markers and a phase-driven ribbon.

items.name: comparison-stage
items.title: Comparison Stage
items.description: Fair side-by-side comparisons of 2D or 3D subjects: renderer-neutral slot layout from real-world extents with one shared px-per-meter and ground line (equal) or declared per-slot fit with ratio badges and scale bars (fit-each), measurements in metric or imperial, tiny-subject diagnostics, matched HeroAssetViewer cameras solved to the planned box with reported perspective residual, and a React view with real-text labels.

items.name: asset-state-sequence
items.title: Asset State Sequence
items.description: Frame-addressed transitions between an asset's supplied states: variant builds (e.g. new/aged/damaged) and pose states driven by real actions; interpolate only where the same build supports it, otherwise explicit crossfade, wipe or cut with transition-fallback diagnostics; unknown states fail at compile time; pure evaluation for any seek order.

items.name: asset-state-sequence-three
items.title: Asset State Sequence (Three.js)
items.description: Composite HeroAsset over supplied variant builds with a single `sequence` action: overlay crossfades for same-shape variants, hashed-alpha dissolves for different shapes, clip-plane wipes, interpolated action poses, unit normalization by metersPerUnit and lazy material clones restored after each transition.

items.name: animated-metric
items.title: Animated Metric
items.description: Deterministic count-ups and changing quantities: currency, percent and unit formats with one precision per metric, interpolate only between known keyframes (MG1 easing) or step for discrete facts, exact rest values, flagged in-between frames, unknown values never zero, change badges colored by declared good direction, and a width reserve so layouts do not jitter.

items.name: measure-units
items.title: Measure Units
items.description: Length, area and angle text from meters in metric or imperial: millimeters and sixteenth-inch fractions for thin layers, ft/in, m²/ft² and roof pitch (rise:12 with degrees).

items.name: dimension-overlay
items.title: Dimension Overlay
items.description: Dimensions, thickness chains, areas, angles and person/bar scale references resolved from asset meters (InspectableAsset anchors and part bounds, or authored values with sources and mismatch checks), projected through any 2D/3D projector with draw-on, upright labels, thin-layer label stacks with leaders, collision avoidance, foreshortening and unplaceable diagnostics; SVG renderer included.

items.name: domain-home-dimensions
items.title: Home Dimensions
items.description: Measured DimensionOverlay specs for a HouseLayout from the same model the 3D build uses: envelope, wall and roof layer stacks, foundation depth, window opening, roof pitch, footprint area and a person for scale.

items.name: mechanism-sequence
items.title: Mechanism Sequence
items.description: Frame-addressed operations on moving parts: rotate/slide with limits, declared part motions, continuous spins with spin-up/down integrated in closed form (real vs visual rpm reported), toggles; after-dependencies with cycle detection, limit clamping and overlap diagnostics; pure per frame.

items.name: mechanism-sequence-three
items.title: Mechanism Sequence (Three.js)
items.description: Applies mechanism joint values to an asset's pivot objects over captured rest transforms: local-axis rotations, spins and slides, declared userData.motion, visibility or emissive toggles; missing pivots fail with the available part list.

items.name: environmental-effects
items.title: Environmental Effects
items.description: Seeded, bounded, always-illustrative rain, storms (gusting wind integrated exactly), blizzards (streaking snow), snow, hail (fall, hop, settle), splashes, dust, drips, condensation, stains and accumulating snow cover: closed-form particles per (seed, index, frame) for exact seeking and fixed memory, capped budgets, fades, reduced-motion variants that keep persistent results; SVG renderer for any 2D projection. Also embers, sparks (one closed-form burst with drag, gravity and a bounce), bokeh, motes that glint only inside a light beam, and fireflies.

items.name: environmental-effects-three
items.title: Environmental Effects (Three.js)
items.description: Fixed-size buffers for rain streaks, soft snow and dust points, instanced water droplets and noisy-edged stain decals, updated per frame and ignored by inspection and section tools.

items.name: fiber-stage
items.title: Fiber Stage
items.description: A React Three Fiber canvas driven by a frame number, for video. It never runs its own loop: each frame renders exactly once after every child has applied it, so any frame in any seek order looks the same, and it marks each frame drawn for the exporter. Children read the frame with useStageFrame; CameraMove adds a slow parallax move.

items.name: environmental-effects-fiber
items.title: Environmental Effects for Fiber
items.description: Rain, snow, dust and the cinematic particles (embers, sparks, bokeh, motes in a light beam, fireflies) as React Three Fiber children of a FiberStage. Every particle is a closed-form function of its seed and the frame, so it seeks exactly with no simulation or bake.

items.name: particle-moments
items.title: Particle Moments
items.description: Ready-made particle moments, each one job done the way film and studio work does it: dust in a shaft of light, rising embers, sparks on an impact frame, lens bokeh, fireflies at dusk, many particles assembling into a mark, and a labelled flow from source to destination. Each comes with its camera move, text timing and sound cues.

items.name: studio-shot-model
items.title: Studio Shot Model
items.description: The specs, camera math and craft checks of the React Three Fiber recipes, with no renderer: hero turns, spotlights, exploded views, comparisons, screens, portals, particles, light through water, baked and captured places, baked physics, and the story scenes (shadow reveal, chain reaction, physical data, tabletop story, scale journey, inside out, diorama journey). `inspectStudioShot`, `inspectLightShot`, `inspectPhysicsShot`, `inspectFlythrough` and `inspectCapturedPlace` run in Node, so a film document is checked before anything loads three.js.

items.name: studio-recipes
items.title: Studio Recipes
items.description: Finished product shots for explainer video in React Three Fiber, each a pure function of the frame: a hero turn that lands on the best angle, a part spotlight with an outline and a measured leader-line label, an exploded view along the assembly axis, a finish comparison and a two-angle proof on one canvas, a push into a screen whose interface performs, a step through a screen into the world it shows, with true parallax and a seamless crossing, and points made with physics (dominoes, stacks) played back from an offline deterministic bake, and particles that gather onto a subject's real surface while it builds in. The subject turns on a turntable inside Kumiki's product studio, with strip, rim, softbox and high-key looks. `inspectStudioShot` checks timing and text against the craft rules.

items.name: splat-stage
items.title: Splat Stage (Captured Place)
items.description: Gaussian-splat captures of real places inside a FiberStage, rendered by Spark (MIT, pinned 2.4.0), exact frame by frame: every frame is held until the capture has loaded and Spark's worker depth sort for that camera has settled, so any frame in any order is identical. CapturedPlace is recipe 12: a slow forward move through the capture, with the licence credit on screen. Optional: the only item that pulls in Spark.

items.name: light-recipes
items.title: Light Recipes
items.description: Light doing something physical, traced rather than painted, as a pure function of the frame. Light Through It: sun on a pool, where a drop's rings focus the light into moving caustics on the floor. `createCaustics` refracts a dense grid of rays through any light-bending mesh (water, glass) onto a floor, with brightness from the change in area and a faint spectral split. `applyCaustics` puts that light inside a floor's own material, so it shows through transmissive water. Real-Light Flythrough: forward through a set whose light was path-traced in Blender Cycles and baked into its textures (`scripts/light-bake.py`), shown unlit.

items.name: domain-home-effects
items.title: Home Effects
items.description: EnvironmentalEffects presets for a HouseLayout: rain, storm, blizzard, snow day (roof and ground cover on the real roof planes), hail, snowfall, a roof leak with a spreading ceiling stain, attic dust and window condensation.

items.name: scalar-field
items.title: Scalar Field Overlay
items.description: Supplied scalar fields (temperature, moisture, pressure) as calibrated colors, contours and threshold bands on any planar surface: explicit unit, source and fixed or dynamic domain, disclosed clipping, hatched missing data (never zero), keyframed fields over time, marching-squares contours; SVG renderer and legend. No physics simulation.

items.name: scalar-field-three
items.title: Scalar Field Overlay (Three.js)
items.description: The field as a translucent data texture on its 3D surface with contour lines, updated per frame and ignored by inspection tools.

items.name: inspect-then-quantify
items.title: Inspect Then Quantify

items.name: failure-cascade
items.title: Failure Cascade
